DOE-UAP-D004, Los Alamos Conference on Aerial Phenomena, 1949
DOE-UAP-D004、航空現象に関するロスアラモス会議、1949 年
Department of Energy
米国エネルギー省
7/10/26
2026年7月10日（Release 04）
3/22/49
New Mexico
ニューメキシコ州
PDF
PDF
This document is a transcript of a 1949 conference held at Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory (now Los Alamos National Laboratory), Los Alamos, New Mexico. Attendees included several eminent scientists and physicists, many of whom had contributed to the development of the first nuclear weapons during the Manhattan Project. The purpose of the conference was to discuss and gather hypotheses to account for the nature and origin of a phenomenon involving “green fireballs” that had been reported over a period of several months in the vicinity of the laboratory. The group did not come to a consensus on a likely attribution for the phenomenon, though a leading hypothesis was that the observations may have been related to meteors entering the atmosphere at a shallow angle and high altitude. Dr. Edward Teller suggested that if not a “material body,” an “electron phenomenon” might be the cause, while Dr. Lincoln LaPaz, an expert specializing in meteorics, expressed that “nothing like this, to [his] knowledge, has ever been observed in the case of meteorite drops.”
この文書は、ニューメキシコ州ロスアラモスのロスアラモス科学研究所（現在のロスアラモス国立研究所）で開催された1949年の会議の記録です。出席者には著名な科学者や物理学者も含まれており、その多くはマンハッタン計画中に最初の核兵器の開発に貢献しました。この会議の目的は、研究所の近くで数ヶ月にわたって報告された「緑色の火の玉」に関連する現象の性質と起源を説明するための仮説を議論し、収集することでした。研究グループは、この現象の可能性の高い原因について意見の一致には至らなかったが、有力な仮説は、この観測が浅い角度と高高度で大気圏に突入する流星に関連している可能性があるというものだった。エドワード・テラー博士は、「物質体」ではないとしても、「電子現象」が原因である可能性があると示唆し、一方、隕石を専門とする専門家であるリンカーン・ラパス博士は、「隕石落下の場合には、[彼の]知る限り、このようなことはこれまで観察されたことがない」と述べた。
既に公開済み

1949年2月16日13:00、ロスアラモス科学研究所会議室P-162で「Aerial Phenomena」会議が開かれた。議題はAR 380-5に基づくSecretに分類され、出席者は適切にクリアランスを受けていた。出席者には第4軍関係者、ネバダ大学のDr. LaPaz、FBI、USAEC担当者、カリフォルニア大学のDr. Bradbury、Dr. Holloway、Dr. Hoyt、Dr. Menley、Dr. Reines、Dr. Tellerらが含まれる。Captain Beetが1948年12月以降の航空会社パイロットからの報告を紹介し、Dr. LaPazが通常の隕石落下と異なる事例を説明した。LaPazは自身が目撃した「Starvation Peak」事件（記載の日時はDecember 12、原文は不確定表記）を報告し、現象は瞬時に最大強度で現れ、波長約5200エングストローム相当の緑〜黄緑色、ほぼ水平に近い軌道で一定角速度で通過し、終端近くで断片化して明るさはほぼ一定、継続時間は約2秒であったと述べた。LaPazは当時ストップウォッチとトランジットを用いて方位・仰角測定を行ったこと、関連報告の完全ファイルが存在することを示した。会議中の一部発言は会場外の騒音で録音が途切れている。
A conference on "Aerial Phenomena" was held 16 February 1949 at 1300 in conference room P-162, Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory. The subject was classified Secret under AR 380-5 and attendees were properly cleared; participants included 4th Army officers, Dr. LaPaz (University of Nevada), FBI, USAEC representatives, and University of California scientists (Dr. Bradbury, Dr. Holloway, Mr. Hoyt, Dr. Menley, Dr. Reines, Dr. Teller). Captain Beet reviewed reports beginning in December 1948 from airline pilots and introduced Dr. LaPaz, who contrasted conventional meteorite falls with observed incidents. Dr. LaPaz described the so-called Starvation Peak incident (date given as December 12 in the text, original has uncertain notation) as appearing instantly at full intensity, color estimated near 5200 Å (green to yellow-green), following an approximately horizontal trajectory at roughly constant angular velocity, fragmenting near the end while remaining bright, and lasting about two seconds. He reported using a stopwatch and a transit to obtain azimuth and elevation measurements and noted that a complete file of reports exists; portions of the record were obscured by external noise.

DOW-UAP-D094, Analysis of Flying Object Incidents in the United States, 1949
DOW-UAP-D094、米国における飛行物体事件の分析、1949 年
Department of War
米国戦争省
7/10/26
2026年7月10日（Release 04）
4/28/49
Virginia
バージニア州
PDF
PDF
This file contains a U.S. Air Force (USAF) Air Intelligence Division study, “Analysis of Flying Object Incidents in the United States,” Study No. 203, dated 04/28/1949. The analysis includes an assessment of various reported unidentified flying object (UFO) incidents and theories to account for their nature and origin. Overall, the study assesses that “it appears that some object has been seen; however, the identification of that object cannot be readily accomplished.” The study offers that two “reasonable” origins might account for the phenomena: technologies of a domestic or foreign origin. It also suggests that, if foreign, it is prudent for the United States to assume that UFO observations are attributable to scientific, military, or intelligence activities of the Soviet Union, and, in that case, to take seriously the threat such objects may pose. The file also contains selected contemporary UFO reports and examples of experimental “flying wing” type aircraft planforms that might account for certain commonly reported UFO characteristics. AARO Comment: This file appears to be a later revision of the file contained in DOW-UAP-D093, whose content is substantively similar.
このファイルには、米国空軍 (USAF) 航空情報部門の調査「米国における飛行物体事件の分析」、調査番号 203、1949 年 4 月 28 日が含まれています。この分析には、報告されているさまざまな未確認飛行物体（UFO）事件の評価と、その性質と起源を説明するための理論が含まれています。全体として、この研究は「何らかの物体が見られたようだが、その物体の特定は容易には達成できない」と評価している。この研究は、国内起源または外国起源の技術という 2 つの「合理的な」起源が現象を説明している可能性があることを示唆しています。また、外国のものであれば、米国にとってUFO観測はソ連の科学活動、軍事活動、または諜報活動によるものであると想定し、その場合、そのような物体がもたらす可能性のある脅威を真剣に受け止めることが賢明であることも示唆している。このファイルには、選択された現代の UFO レポートと、一般的に報告されている特定の UFO の特徴を説明できるかもしれない実験的な「全翼型」タイプの航空機の平面図の例も含まれています。 AARO コメント: このファイルは、DOW-UAP-D093 に含まれるファイルの新しいリビジョンであるようで、その内容は実質的に類似しています。

文書名: Air Intelligence Division Study No.203（1948年12月10日、Air Intelligence Report No.100-203-79）。目的は「flying saucers（以下 flying objects）」の戦術的パターンを検討し存在可能性を評価すること。報告は約210件の事案を集計し、米気象局職員、USAF将校、民間パイロット等の訓練された観測者による報告が含まれる点を指摘する。目撃記述は主に三類（銀色円盤/球、粗い葉巻形、火の玉）に分類され、視角や条件の違いで単一物体が異様に見えた可能性も示唆される。国内起源の候補として気球、ロケット、実験的飛行翼機（XF5U-1、Northrup B-35、YB-49、過去のArup機等）が挙げられ、同様に外国（主としてソ連）起源の可能性も検討される。ソ連がホルテン型等の飛行翼に関心を持ち、Guenther Bockを利用しているとする情報や低評価情報としてホルテン機部隊に関する報告が記されている。推奨事項として、国内発射記録の調査と各機関の協力による識別努力が不可欠であり、国内説明が否定されれば外国起源として脅威扱いし、識別・迎撃のためより積極的な対処を正当化する旨が結論として示される。付録に目撃分布図（付録B）や選定事例、飛行翼機の資料が含まれる。
Document: Air Intelligence Division Study No.203 (Air Intelligence Report No.100-203-79), 10 December 1948. Purpose: examine tactics attributed to "flying saucers" ("flying objects") and assess their possible existence. Approximately 210 incidents were collected, including reports from trained observers such as U.S. Weather Bureau personnel, USAF officers, experienced civilian pilots and technicians. Descriptions fall into three categories—disk/ball, rough cigar-shaped, and balls of fire—with the report noting that viewing angle and conditions could make a single type appear differently. Domestic explanations considered include weather balloons, rockets, and experimental flying‑wing aircraft (e.g., XF5U‑1, Northrop B‑35, YB‑49, earlier Arup tailless design); foreign (primarily Soviet) origin is also considered, with mention of Soviet interest in flying‑wing designs, use of Dr. Guenther Bock, and low‑evaluation reports about Horten-type units. Conclusions call for interagency cooperation and a survey of domestic launches to confirm or deny domestic origins; if domestic explanations are ruled out, the objects should be treated as potential foreign threats warranting identification and interception. Appendices include a sightings map (Appendix B), selected incident reports and material on flying‑wing aircraft.

This file contains an initial report from the Air Materiel Command regarding Project Sign. Project Sign was a 1948-1949 U.S. Air Force program to investigate the nature and origin of unidentified flying objects (UFO). The report details 100 UFO sightings from 1947-1948. The file also contains an article excerpted from “The Aeroplane,” an aviation-focused periodical magazine published between 1911 and 1968, titled “The Biology of the Flying Saucer.”
このファイルには、プロジェクト・サインに関する航空資材軍団からの最初の報告書が含まれています。プロジェクト・サインは、未確認飛行物体 (UFO) の性質と起源を調査するための 1948 年から 1949 年のアメリカ空軍プログラムでした。この報告書は、1947年から1948年にかけて100件のUFO目撃情報を詳述している。このファイルには、1911 年から 1968 年にかけて発行された航空専門の定期雑誌「The Aeroplane」から抜粋された「空飛ぶ円盤の生物学」というタイトルの記事も含まれています。

本書は1947年12月30日付の指示（General L. C. Craigie署名）にもとづく未確認飛行物体に関する初期報告である。報告ではプロジェクトHT-304が1948年1月26日に活性化され、1948年2月11日付Technical Instruction 2185が発行されたこと、報告はHQ, AMCおよびUSAF諜報部長からの転送資料を統合したものであると記されている。夜間点灯広告飛行船の運航予定は照合済みである。添付1は1948年2月1日までの報告集計で、観察上の共通点として高い上昇率や静止・ホバリングのように見える挙動、楕円・円盤・ソーサー形の記述、付随音の報告、サイズ報告の幅（コイン大〜直径260フィート、戦闘機大〜B-29数機相当）、目撃あたりの数（単独77件、2–6個21件、6–10個8件、10超9件）、排気痕23件、速度はホバリング〜超音速の全域が挙げられている。添付2・5は事故番号40の写真拡大、添付4はその評価であり、複数の添付間に顕著な類似性があるとする。代表者はGE研究所のDr. Irving Langmuirと面談し、現時点の資料は肯定的な同定に不十分であるとの見解を得ている。Langmuirは「飛行円盤」を実在とすることに慎重だったが、本司令部は境界層制御を用いた低アスペクト比機体により報告の外観・性能の多くを再現できる可能性があると記している。添付目録（6点）と多数の事例表がある。
This document is an initial report on unidentified flying objects directed by a 30 December 1947 letter signed by General L. C. Craigie. It notes Project HT-304 was activated on 26 January 1948 and Technical Instruction 2185 was published 11 February 1948; the file consolidates reports received by HQ, AMC and those forwarded by the USAF Director of Intelligence. Schedules of lighted night-flying advertising blimps were checked. Enclosure 1 is a tabulation through 1 February 1948. Common observations include high climb rates and apparent ability to hover, frequent descriptions as oval/disc/saucer, associated sound reported, reported sizes ranging from coin-size to 260 feet (and from pursuit-plane size to the bulk of six B-29s), distribution of objects per sighting (77 single, 21 with 2–6, 8 with 6–10, 9 with over 10), exhaust trails reported 23 times, and speeds estimated from very slow/hovering to supersonic. Enclosures 2 and 5 are enlargements of photos of Incident #40; enclosure 4 is an evaluation of enclosure 2 and similarities among enclosures are noted. Headquarters representatives consulted Dr. Irving Langmuir (GE Research Laboratories), who judged available data insufficient for positive identification and was reluctant to treat “flying discs” as real. Headquarters states it is possible a low-aspect-ratio aircraft using boundary-layer control could duplicate many reported appearance and performance characteristics. Six enclosures and a detailed incident table are included.

This memorandum summarizes a Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) debriefing of a group of four individuals who reported observing a “flying saucer” or “unconventional aircraft” in 1955. The group, which included U.S. Senator Richard Russell, a U.S. military service member, and two U.S. Government officials, reported observing a luminescent “greenish-yellow” phenomenon, as seen from aboard a train while traveling within the Soviet Union, in present-day Azerbaijan, between Baku and Tiflis (Tbilisi, Georgia). The document concludes by stating that the observation can “probably be explained as steep climbing aircraft or missiles,” and that “the evidence does not appear sufficiently firm to warrant the conclusion that the Soviets have developed […] a radically new type of aircraft.” The document “CIA-UAP-D021” contains a contemporary analysis of the incident.

Sections 1 and 2 of this memorandum document a 1955 analysis of reports of “flying saucers” or “unconventional aircraft,” referencing the incident described in observer debriefings contained within CIA-UAP-D020. The memo summarizes the incident as consisting of two lights rising vertically, then passing above the observers. The memo contains caveating language that suggests the author concluded that the reports, as described, did not indicate the presence of an “unconventional aircraft.” Section 3 cites a previous finding by Dr. [Howard] Robertson (of the 1953 Robertson Panel) that “almost all the sightings […] represented no threat to the U.S.” Section 4 discusses the state of then-current research into “saucer-like aircraft” under Project “Y,” a contemporary joint U.S.-Canadian aerospace development program.

The cover letter presents this as the Pantex Unidentified Object report for September 2, 2015, while the incident narrative states that on September 1, 2015 at approximately 0710 hours the Ground Surveillance Radar (GSR) detected an unknown object west of Pantex moving north in a non‑threatening manner. Protective Force (PF) responded per the NPO UAS incident response plan; pedestrian and vehicle gates were secured and patrols positioned. A PF lieutenant and a Security Police Officer (SPO) visually tracked the object (attempted interception), observed no sound or visible propulsion, and described a diamond‑type shape with a rounder top. The object was followed for several miles north, last seen near County Road G and F.M. 1342; observers reported the object increased speed and changed direction, last known heading ENE. A Bearcat with a CROWS camera tracked the object at an estimated 100–200 ft altitude for 3–5 minutes at about 75–100 m distance. Size estimates were ~4 ft tall by ~2 ft wide at the base; color reports were inconsistent (black, silver, red, blue). Video from the nearest GSR tower—limited in detail due to distance—was sent to Sandia National Labs for analysis and enhanced images are included in the report. The object did not appear threatening nor did it approach sensitive assets. All evidence (statements, video, etc.) was turned over to an FBI agent.

This report accompanies the video titled “DOW-UAP-PR106.” A U.S. military operator reported observing an object, describing it as “quite small” and as “continu[ing] in a constant direction.” The report characterizes the shape of the phenomenon as “indistinguishable,” with a metallic appearance and reflective underside. This file documents the 1966-1967 deliberations and recommendations of the U.S. Air Force (USAF) Scientific Advisory Board’s Ad Hoc Committee to Review Project Blue Book. Project Blue Book was a 1952-1969 USAF program to investigate the nature and origin of unidentified flying objects (UFO). The Committee recommended that the USAF contract a scientific team composed of university-affiliated representatives to investigate selected UFO sightings. The USAF subsequently adopted the Committee’s recommendation.

This file contains a U.S. Air Force (USAF) Air Intelligence Division study, “Analysis of Flying Object Incidents in the United States,” Study No. 203, dated 12/10/1948. The analysis includes an assessment of various reported unidentified flying object (UFO) incidents and theories to account for their nature and origin. Overall, the study assesses that “it appears that some object has been seen; however, the identification of that object cannot be readily accomplished.” The study offers that two “reasonable” origins might account for the phenomena: technologies of a domestic or foreign origin. It also suggests that, if foreign, it is prudent for the United States to assume that UFO observations are attributable to scientific, military, or intelligence activities of the Soviet Union, and, in that case, to take seriously the threat such objects may pose. The file also contains contemporary UFO reports and examples of experimental “flying wing” type aircraft planforms that might account for certain commonly reported UFO characteristics. AARO Comment: This file appears to be an earlier draft version of the file contained in DOW-UAP-D094, whose content is substantively similar.

1948年12月10日付の報告。目的は、米国内で報告された「飛行物体（Flying Saucer等）」の起源と実在性を検討すること。約210件の報告があり、気象観測員、米空軍の有資格操縦士、経験ある民間操縦士、技術者など訓練・経験ある観測者の報告を含む。観測記述は大きく（1）円盤状、（2）円形の翼状、（3）球状等に分類され、視角や条件の差で同一物が異って報告される可能性が指摘される。報告地域は大西洋岸や五大湖周辺が多い。可能な説明として気象気球、ロケット、通常航空機、天文現象等のほか、外国（特にソ連）起源の飛行翼型機やドイツ由来設計の影響が検討される。ソ連関与の目的としては（a）原爆への信頼低下、（b）撮影偵察、（c）米防空の試験、（d）慣熟飛行等が列挙される。結論としては、米空軍が関係機関と協力して国内起源の可能性を確実に除外できない限り、これらを脅威として扱い、識別・迎撃等のより積極的な調査を行う必要がある。付属資料（Appendices A–D等）あり。
Report dated 10 December 1948 analyzing the origin and existence of reported flying objects ("flying saucers") in the United States. Approximately 210 incidents were reported, including accounts from trained and experienced observers such as weather observers, USAF-rated pilots, experienced civilian pilots, and technicians. Descriptions were grouped roughly into (1) disk-shaped, (2) round-winged, and (3) ball/spherical types; the report notes that viewing conditions and angles could cause the same object to be reported under different types. Sightings were concentrated along the Atlantic coast and the Great Lakes area. Possible explanations considered include weather balloons, rockets, conventional aircraft, celestial phenomena, and foreign-origin devices—particularly Soviet interest in flying-wing designs and German-derived aircraft (e.g., Horten types). Potential Soviet motives listed are: (a) undermine U.S. confidence in the atomic bomb, (b) conduct photographic reconnaissance, (c) test U.S. air defenses, and (d) perform familiarization flights. Conclusion: the USAF should coordinate with other agencies; if domestic explanations cannot be firmly established, the objects should be treated as a potential threat warranting more active identification and interception efforts. Appendices A–D provide detailed analyses and selected reports.

This file contains reports, memoranda, and correspondence concerning various then-developmental vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) aircraft. The file includes assessments of the experimental potential of the “Avro Project Y2,” a joint U.S.-Canadian near-circular VTOL aircraft that is similar in appearance to contemporary popular descriptions of unidentified flying objects (UFO). A 1954 memorandum opines that VTOL aircraft with a circular planform may be mistaken for UFOs to observers unfamiliar with such technologies. It also recommends that UFO reports in the vicinity of Soviet military operations or assets be re-examined to assess whether they may be attributable to previously unknown advanced VTOL aircraft of foreign design. The file also contains correspondence relating to a UFO incident involving a U.S. Air Force (USAF) KC-97 flying near Newfoundland, Canada in July 1955. A USAF committee found that the characteristics described in the report were inconsistent with those of known Soviet, American, or Canadian military systems. The committee was also “unable to explain the simultaneous ground radar returns and aircrew visual sightings.” It also contains correspondence relating to the potential value of data from incidental radar collection of meteors entering the atmosphere. USAF Air Research and Development Command recommended using that data to improve the performance of the AN/FPS-17 radar system. Finally, the file contains correspondence indicating support for the Communications Instructions for Reporting Vital Intelligence Sightings (CIRVIS) program, a joint U.S.-Canadian civil-military program to standardize reporting methods for unusual or unidentified airborne and maritime hazards and threats.

In the recording, crew members and debriefers discuss the “light flash phenomena,” a then novel, now well-documented biological effect where high-energy cosmic rays pass through the eye and strike the retina, causing the perception of light streaks or flashes.
